Che Guevara (14 June 1928 - 9 October 1967) was an Argentine Marxist revolutionary, author, guerrilla leader, diplomat, politician, and military theorist.
This Swedish diplomat became the youngest person ever elected UN Secretary-General at just 47, serving from 1953 until his death in a 1961 plane crash — who is he?

Dag Hammarskjöld (29 July 1905 - 18 September 1961) was a Swedish economist and diplomat who served as the second Secretary-General of the United Nations from April 1953 until his death in a plane crash in September 1961.

Dorians were one of the four major ethnic groups into which the Hellenes (or Greeks) of Classical Greece divided themselves (along with the Aeolians, Achaeans, and Ionians).

Ernest Shackleton (15 February 1874 - 5 January 1922) was an Anglo-Irish Antarctic explorer who led three British expeditions to the Antarctic.
The only Central African president born in modern-day Gabon, this former army chief led the country from 2003 to 2013 — who is he?
François Bozizé (born 14 October 1946) is a Central African politician who was President of the Central African Republic from 2003 to 2013.

Giuseppe Garibaldi (4 July 1807 - 2 June 1882) was an Italian general, revolutionary and republican.
As China's top leader on Hong Kong and Macau affairs, this former Shanghai mayor rose to the Politburo Standing Committee before becoming vice president in 2023 — who is he?
Han Zheng (pinyin: Hn Zhng; born April 1955) is a Chinese politician who, since 2023, has served as the 11th vice president of China.
Traced to Gustav Fechner's 1854 sensory-judgment theories and Wilhelm Wundt's founding of the first dedicated research lab in Leipzig in 1879 — this is the origin story of which scientific field?
History of psychology is defined as "the scientific study of behavior and mental processes".

Generally hailed as the first major investment banker in the United States, he helped finance the Union war effort and then the postwar push of railroads into the Northwest — who was he?

Jay Cooke (August 10, 1821 - February 16, 1905) was an American financier who helped finance the Union war effort during the American Civil War and the postwar development of railroads in the northwestern United States.

Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya (born 28 November 1941) is a Mauritanian military officer and politician who served as the President of Mauritania from 1984 to 2005.
Raised Anglican though her parents converted to Catholicism, which queen ruled Britain jointly with her husband William from 1689 until her death in 1694?
Mary II (30 April 1662 - 28 December 1694) was Queen of England, Scotland, and Ireland with her husband, King William III and II, from 1689 until her death in 1694.
Formerly head of the Federal Taxation Service, this economist became Russia's prime minister in 2020 after Dmitry Medvedev's government resigned. Who is he?

France's longest-serving head of state across 22 years, he was the country's second president and its very last monarch, deposed in 1870 — who was he?

Sanskrit for 'circle,' this geometric configuration of symbols is used across Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, and Shinto traditions to aid meditation and represent sacred space — what is it?

William Pitt the Younger: British statesman (1759–1806)
This Korean admiral won all of his roughly 23 naval battles against Japan, most famously defeating a fleet of over 130 ships with just 13 of his own — who is he?
A dispute between two rival lords escalated into a decade-long Japanese civil war from 1467 to 1477 that triggered the Warring States period — what was this conflict called?
Ōnin War: 15th-century civil war in Japan.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Saint Valentine (born 175) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
SQL (founded 1974) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four. MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Who among these is a chemist?
Stephanie Kwolek is a chemist. Stephanie Louise Kwolek (July 31, 1923 – June 18, 2014) was a Polish-American chemist known for inventing Kevlar (poly-paraphenylene terephthalamide).
What is the atomic number of Tennessine?
Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.
What is the atomic number of Astatine?
Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.
In what year did Tomitaro Makino die?
Tomitaro Makino (牧野 富太郎, Makino Tomitarō; 24 April 1862 – 18 January 1957) was a pioneer Japanese botanist noted for his taxonomic work.
In what year was Aluminium discovered?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
Which company manufactures Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: Skunk Works. The SR-71 was developed in the 1960s as a black project by Lockheed's Skunk Works division.
Which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 from?

Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19: Soviet Union. The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 (Russian: Микоян и Гуревич МиГ-19; NATO reporting name: Farmer) is a Soviet second generation, single-seat, twinjet fighter aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Pyxis?
Pyxis: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Pyxis is a small and faint constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Neodymium?
Neodymium: Carl Auer von Welsbach. Neodymium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nd and atomic number 60.
Who is credited with discovering TON 618?
Who is credited with discovering Thallium?
Thallium: Claude-Auguste Lamy. Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
A "classic organochlorine" insecticide once heavily used to treat seed and soil, it was banned in most countries by the 1990s after proving a persistent, bioaccumulating pollutant. What is it?
Aldrin is an organochlorine insecticide that was widely used until the 1990s, when it was banned in most countries.
This order of ray-finned fish is named for a modified fin ray that dangles like bait to lure in prey, much like a human with a fishing rod — what are they called?

Anglerfish are ray-finned fish in the order Lophiiformes. The majority are bottom-dwellers, being demersal fish, while the aberrant deep-sea anglerfish are pelagic, (mostly) living high in the water column.
Jointed legs, a chitin exoskeleton they must moult to grow, and haemolymph instead of blood mark which wildly diverse group of invertebrates?
Arthropod are invertebrates in the phylum Arthropoda.
Grown for its edible taproot in red or golden varieties and closely related to Swiss chard, this vegetable's leaves are eaten too, sold simply as "greens" — which root vegetable?
Beetroot is the taproot portion of a Beta vulgaris subsp.
The third-most-produced bomber in history, this American four-engine heavy bomber dominated the European Theater and dropped more bombs than any other plane in WWII — which aircraft is it?
Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress is an American four-engined heavy bomber aircraft that was developed in the mid-1930s for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC).

Synthesized by the liver in response to inflammation, this ring-shaped blood molecule binds to the surface of dead or dying cells to activate the immune system's complement cascade. What is it commonly called?
C-reactive protein (CRP) is an annular (ring-shaped) pentameric protein found in blood plasma, whose circulating concentration rises in response to inflammation.
A flightless ratite native to the tropical forests of New Guinea and northeastern Australia, this large bird has three living species and lacks a keel on its breastbone — name the bird?
Cassowary (Tok) are flightless birds of the genus Casuarius, in the order Casuariiformes.
Made of DNA wound around histone proteins, this substance shapes chromosomes into their distinctive forms during cell division and gatekeeps access to genes for transcription and repair — what is it?
Chromatin is a complex of DNA and protein responsible for condensing and packaging chromosomal DNA.
With algorithms and data structures at its core and the theory of computation among its branches, which field studies computation, information, and automation?

Computer science is the study of computation, information, and automation. The theory of computation concerns abstract models of computation and general classes of problems that can be solved using them.
Present in the cytoplasm of bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotic cells alike, this dynamic protein-filament network stabilizes tissue and enables cells to migrate — what is it?
Cytoskeleton is a complex, dynamic network of interlinking protein filaments present in the cytoplasm of all cells, including those of bacteria and archaea.

Derived from the wild rock dove and split into more than 350 distinct breeds, this domesticated bird was already being bred by Mesopotamians more than 5,000 years ago, according to cuneiform tablets — what's the bird?
Domestic pigeon (Columba livia "domestica" or Columba livia forma domestica) is a domesticated bird derived from the rock dove (Columba livia), of which it is also a subspecies.
This is the earliest developmental stage of a multicellular organism, beginning with a single-celled zygote formed just after fertilization — what is it called?
Embryo is the initial stage of development for a multicellular organism.
This sensory organ detects light and converts it into electro-chemical signals in neurons, using an adjustable lens system to focus incoming light and form images — name the organ?
Eye is a sensory organ that allows an organism to perceive visual information.
This Italian-American economist, who taught at MIT's Sloan School, took home the 1985 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics. Who was he?
Franco Modigliani (18 June 1918 - 25 September 2003) was an Italian-American economist and the recipient of the 1985 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics.
The most aggressive and common cancer to originate in the brain, this tumor is thought to arise from cells called astrocytes and carries a grim prognosis — what is it?
Glioblastoma (GBM), is the most aggressive and most common type of cancer that originates in the brain, and has a very poor prognosis for survival.
The first Professor of the Public Understanding of Mathematics at Cambridge, she's also a BBC broadcaster who explores the math behind human relationships — who is she?
Hannah Fry (born 21 February 1984) is a British mathematician, author and broadcaster.
This common household insect, likely originating in the Middle East, mates only once in her lifetime but stores the sperm to fertilize repeated batches of about 100 eggs — what insect is it?
Housefly (Musca domestica) is a fly of the suborder Cyclorrhapha.
Patented in 1961 and approved two years later, this nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug works by blocking the enzyme cyclooxygenase to cut prostaglandin production — what drug is it?
Indometacin is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) commonly used as a prescription medication to reduce fever, pain, stiffness, and swelling from inflammation.
This self-described 'constitutional law attorney' joined Trump's inner circle in November 2019, though reporters found she'd never argued a federal case — who is she?
Jenna Ellis (born November 1, 1984) is an American conservative suspended lawyer who was a member of Donald Trump's 2020 re-election campaign's legal team.
Found from Africa to the Americas, this family of 118 bird species has big heads and sharp bills, and though most picture them by rivers, many actually live deep in forests — what are they?
Kingfisher are a family, the Alcedinidae, of small to medium-sized, brightly coloured birds in the order Coraciiformes.
Used to treat an underactive thyroid and even a severe form called myxedema coma, this synthetic version of thyroxine (T4) takes about six weeks to reach a steady blood level — what's this drug?
Levothyroxine is a synthetic form of the thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4). It is used to treat thyroid hormone deficiency (hypothyroidism), including a severe form known as myxedema coma.
The sole species in its genus, this South Chinese fruit has a sweet, mildly tart flavor and a distinctive rose-like floral aroma — name it?
Lychee (US also) are the fruit of the tree Litchi chinensis, the sole member of the genus Litchi, part of the soapberry family, Sapindaceae.
This genus of flowering plants belongs to the chamomile tribe of the sunflower family, and several of its species go by the folk name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Matricaria is a genus of flowering plants in the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family.

Usually white but sometimes tinged yellow or pink, this liquid food produced by mammary glands is the primary source of nutrition for young mammals, with its very first production called colostrum — name the substance?
Milk is usually a white liquid food (but can be shades of yellow, cream, pink, or brown) produced by the mammary glands of lactating mammals.

This condition, an inflammation of the heart muscle itself, can cause shortness of breath, chest pain, and irregular heartbeat, and may progress to heart failure if it leads to chronic remodeling of the heart — name the condition?

Myocarditis is inflammation of the cardiac muscle. Myocarditis can progress to inflammatory cardiomyopathy when there is associated ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction due to chronic inflammation.

Introduced in 2001 and operated by the U.S. Air Force, this high-altitude, remotely piloted surveillance aircraft uses synthetic aperture radar and infrared sensors for long-endurance reconnaissance missions — name the aircraft?

Northrop Grumman RQ-4 Global Hawk is a high-altitude, remotely-piloted surveillance aircraft introduced in 2001. It was initially designed by Ryan Aeronautical (now part of Northrop Grumman), and known as Tier II+ during development.
It surges during childbirth and sexual activity, drives maternal bonding and milk production, and is released by the posterior pituitary — which hormone is this?
Oxytocin is a peptide hormone and neuropeptide normally produced in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.
This inflammation of the lining of the abdominal cavity can be caused by a ruptured appendix, a perforated ulcer, or pancreatitis, and may lead to shock if untreated. What condition is it?
Peritonitis is inflammation of the localized or generalized peritoneum, the lining of the inner wall of the abdomen and covering of the abdominal organs.
Caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and often spread by flea bites, this disease comes in pneumonic, bubonic, and septicemic forms — what is it?
Plague (disease) is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. There are three forms of plague, each affecting a different part of the body and causing associated symptoms.
Roaming the interior of western and central North America, this even-toed mammal survived the Pleistocene extinction of its close relatives and evolved to resemble an antelope — which creature is it?
Pronghorn (Antilocapra americana) is a species of artiodactyl (even-toed, hoofed) mammal indigenous to interior western and central North America.

Distinguished from their smaller rodent cousins mainly by size, these long-tailed rodents span dozens of genera worldwide, with Rattus being the most familiar — of the 56 known species, what are they collectively called?
Rat are various medium-sized, long-tailed rodents.

Originally bred in Germany to herd livestock and pull carts of butchered meat to market until railways took over in the mid-1800s, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog now also works as a guard and police dog - name the breed?
Rottweiler (UK also) is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.
Most episodes of this brain-activity disruption last under two minutes and leave the person confused or fatigued afterward, but one lasting over five minutes is a medical emergency — what is it?
Seizure is a sudden disruption of brain activity caused by excessive, synchronized neuronal firing that results in changes in behavior.
With the formula CH3COONa, this colorless, moisture-absorbing salt of acetic acid is deliquescent, meaning it can even dissolve in the water it pulls from the air — which compound?
Sodium acetate is a chemical compound with formula CH3COONa, also abbreviated NaOAc.

This medical emergency occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is blocked or reduced, causing cell death — its warning signs include facial drooping and sudden difficulty speaking or moving one side of the body. Name the condition?

Stroke is a medical condition in which blood flow to a part of the brain is reduced or blocked causing cell death. There are two main types of stroke: ischemic, due to lack of blood flow, and hemorrhagic, due to bleeding.
Sporting beaded antennae and a pale, soft-bodied worker caste, these decaying-wood eaters belong to the order Isoptera and are really highly derived cockroaches — what are they?
Termite are a group of eusocial insects which consume a variety of decaying plant material, generally in the form of wood, leaf litter, and soil humus.
Caused by superantigens from staph or strep bacteria, this condition brings fever, a sunburn-like rash, and peeling skin, and has been tied to absorbent tampon use — which condition?
Toxic shock syndrome (TSS) is a condition caused by bacterial toxins.
This abnormal enlargement of the vein network draining the testicles is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, found in over a third of men with the condition. Name it?
Varicocele is an abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform venous plexus in the scrotum.

This bird family, which also includes piculets, wrynecks, and sapsuckers, is absent from Australia and Madagascar, though one desert-dwelling member has adapted to drill into cacti — what family of birds is it?
Woodpecker are part of the bird family Picidae, which also includes the piculets, wrynecks, and sapsuckers.
The simplest and smallest ketone, this colorless, pungent, highly flammable liquid mixes freely with water and lurks in nail polish remover and paint thinner — what is it?
Working at Baghdad's House of Wisdom around 820, this Islamic Golden Age scholar wrote a treatise whose Arabic title, Al-Jabr, gave us the very word "algebra." Who was he?
Sometimes called 'pigweed,' this genus of plants is grown worldwide as a leaf vegetable and for its edible grain — which genus?
Amaranth: Genus of plants. The plant can grow from 1 to 2.5 metres (3 to 8 feet) tall with a succulent, hollow stem.
Comprising the talocrural, subtalar, and inferior tibiofibular joints, this region where the foot meets the leg enables dorsiflexion and plantarflexion — which body part?
Ankle: Region where the foot and the leg meet. The ankle includes three joints: the ankle joint proper or talocrural joint, the subtalar joint, and the inferior tibiofibular joint.
Also called gobō, this Eurasian plant is cultivated in Japan for its edible root but has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils elsewhere — which species?
Arctium lappa: Species of flowering plant. It has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils in North America, Australia, and other regions, but is cultivated for its vegetable root.

Also called the moon jellyfish, this once-thought-cosmopolitan species was split into roughly 28 separate species in the 2020s and is now known to live only in the north Atlantic and off Argentina — which species?
Aurelia aurita: Species of jellyfish. The species now identified as A. aurita is only found in the north Atlantic and in Argentina, and is not dangerous to humans.

This relationship, expressed as A = εcl, links how much light a solution absorbs directly to its concentration — what is this principle called, named after two scientists whose work dates back to the mid-18th century?
Beer–Lambert law: Scientific law describing absorption of light.
Long-tailed and originally from the Indian subcontinent, this whiskered rodent is a major agricultural pest yet is honored as sacred at the Karni Mata Temple in India — which species is it?
Black rat: Species of rodent. It is a generalist omnivore that can live on a wide variety of foods.
Distinguished by a cube-shaped body, this class of stinging cnidarians includes species such as Chironex fleckeri, whose venom is often fatal to humans — what is it?
Box jellyfish: Class of cnidarians distinguished by their cube-shaped medusae.
Developed in 1964 at Britain's Royal Radar Establishment and influenced by JOVIAL, this programming language was chosen by the UK Ministry of Defence in 1971 for military applications — what is it?
CORAL: Early programming language. The R was originally for "radar", not "real-time".
Derived from Greek words for 'heart' and 'study,' this branch of internal medicine covers coronary artery disease, heart failure, and electrophysiology — which medical field?
Cardiology: Branch of medicine dealing with the heart.
Triggered by anything from a stroke to a bout of altitude sickness, this dangerous buildup of fluid inside the skull raises pressure on brain tissue and can cause seizures or worse — what is it?
Cerebral edema: Excess accumulation of fluid in the brain.
This class of jawed fish — including sharks, rays, skates, and ghost-like chimaeras — has skeletons made entirely of cartilage rather than bone — what is it called?
Chondrichthyes: Class of jawed cartilaginous fish. Chondrichthyes are aquatic vertebrates with paired fins, paired nares, placoid scales, and conus arteriosus in the heart.
Nicknamed the 'palm thief,' this giant terrestrial arthropod can weigh over 9 pounds, making it the largest land-dwelling arthropod alive today — what is it?
With a long hooked bill and webbing between all four toes, this fish-eating aquatic bird family includes the 'great' species commonly seen around Britain and Ireland — what are they called?
Cormorant: Family of aquatic birds. The common names "cormorant" and "shag" have been assigned to different species in the family somewhat haphazardly.
Sometimes called 'bipolar III,' this mood disorder involves cycling periods of mild depression and elevated mood that never reach the severity of full manic or depressive episodes — what is it?
Cyclothymia: Mental disorder. Cyclothymia differs from bipolar disorder in the fact that major depression and mania are not found.
Whether for an object, a process, or a system, this is the intentional concept or proposal created by a thinking agent, balancing purpose, aesthetics, and constraints — what single word names it?
Design: Plan for the construction of an object or system.
Brought to Australia as an infant, this geologist joined Shackleton's Nimrod Expedition and became a leading figure of the Heroic Age of Antarctic exploration — who is it?
Douglas Mawson: Australian geologist and explorer of the Antarctic (1882–1958)
This membrane-bound series of protein complexes shuttles electrons through redox reactions, building a proton gradient that ultimately powers the synthesis of ATP — what's it called?
Electron transport chain: Energy-producing metabolic pathway.
Named from the Greek for 'red skin,' this bacterial infection produces a raised, sharply defined, bright-red rash typically on the face or legs — what's the condition?
Erysipelas: Human disease from a bacterial infection of the skin.
Also nicknamed the 'baum' or 'sweet' variety, this mustelid species ranges across much of the continent into Asia Minor, the Caucasus, and parts of Iran, Iraq, and Syria. What animal is it?
European pine marten: Species of mammal in the mustelid family.
Found on the forelimbs of most tetrapods, these prehensile, often opposable digits give primates like humans their dexterity for grasping and fine movement — what are they called?

Making up roughly 88% of all living amphibians, this short-bodied, tailless order gets its name from Ancient Greek for 'without tail' — and its warty-skinned members are casually dubbed toads. What is it?
Frog: Order of amphibians. The eggs then hatch into fully aquatic larvae called tadpoles, which have tails and internal gills.
First described by J. D. Hooker in 1889 and nicknamed the Transvaal or Barberton daisy for its South African origins, what genus of flowering plant is this?
Gerbera: Genus of plants. Gerbera ( JUR-bər-ə or GUR-bər-ə) L. is a genus of plants in the Asteraceae (Compositae) family.
This cluster of immune cells forms around bacteria, fungi, or foreign material the body can't otherwise clear away — what is it called?
Granuloma: Inflammatory aggregation of immune cells.

This British aviation entrepreneur held three Guinness World Records after visiting the South Pole, the Challenger Deep, and space, then died in 2023 aboard the submersible that imploded near the Titanic wreck — who was he?
Using only a triangle's three side lengths and their semiperimeter, this ancient geometric method computes the triangle's area — what is it known as?
Heron's formula: Triangle area in terms of side lengths.
Generally colourless, hydrophobic, and faintly gasoline-scented, which organic compound is made entirely of hydrogen and carbon and includes everything from methane to paraffin wax?

Hydrocarbon: Organic compound consisting entirely of hydrogen and carbon. In the fossil fuel industries, hydrocarbon refers to naturally occurring petroleum, natural gas and coal, or their hydrocarbon derivatives and purified forms.
Powered by four Aviadvigatel turbofans and built in Voronezh, this Soviet-designed wide-body jet now serves mainly as the Russian president's aircraft — which airliner?
Ilyushin Il-96: Russian four-engined long-range wide-body jet airliner.
Resembling a mustelid despite being a wild cat, this Americas-native feline comes in gray or red color morphs and once roamed as far north as Texas — which species?
Jaguarundi: Species of felid. Its range extends from central Argentina in the south and much of South America east of the Andes, through Central America, and into northern Mexico.
He wrote the first commercial anti-virus software in 1987, then later urged people to uninstall the product bearing his name and twice ran for U.S. president — who was he?
John McAfee: British and American programmer and businessman (1945–2021)
With an average length of 3.18 to 4 meters and a record of 5.85 meters, this snake is the world's longest venomous species, endemic to Asia. What is it?
King cobra: Group of venomous snakes from Asia.
Closely related to earthworms but equipped with a sucker at each end, these segmented worms are mostly freshwater dwellers, and the medicinal species famously feeds on blood — what are they?
Leech: Parasitic or predatory annelid worms.
A Chinese computer engineer turned science-fiction author, he won the Hugo Award for The Three-Body Problem and the Locus Award for its sequel, Death's End. Who is he?
Liu Cixin: Chinese science fiction writer (born 1963)
Developed by MathWorks and named for its focus on matrix manipulations, this proprietary numeric computing environment powers the add-on Simulink for model-based design. What's it called?
MATLAB: Numerical computing environment and programming language.
Whether a milk board's 'Got Milk?' campaign or a city pitching itself as a tourist destination, this discipline boils down to acquiring, satisfying, and retaining customers — what is it?
Marketing: Study and process of exploring, creating, and delivering value to customers.
More than 80% of cases of this cancer — which grows in the thin lining covering the lungs and other organs — trace back to asbestos exposure. What is it?
Produced by mammary glands and rich in calcium, protein and lactose, this liquid is often prized for its antibody-packed early form, colostrum — what is it?
Milk: Nutrient-rich liquid produced by mammals.
Named for a Tanzanian teenager who studied it scientifically in the 1960s, this puzzling phenomenon claims hot liquids can sometimes freeze faster than cold ones — what is it called?
Mpemba effect: Natural phenomenon that hot water freezes faster than cold.

Nicknamed the 'flesh-eating disease' even though the bacteria don't actually consume tissue — they release toxins that kill it instead — this fast-spreading infection often enters through a cut or burn. What condition is it?
Necrotizing fasciitis: Infection that results in the death of the body's soft tissue.
A subsonic flying wing with a crew of two to three, this nuclear-capable stealth aircraft was built to slip past sophisticated air defenses for the US Air Force — what is it?
Northrop B-2 Spirit: American heavy strategic bomber.

Sitting between tissue and a full body system in life's hierarchy, this general term describes a structural unit built from functional tissue (parenchyma) plus supportive tissue (stroma), as seen in the intestinal wall — what is such a unit called?
Organ (biology): Collection of tissues with similar functions.
This skin sensation includes the classic 'pins and needles' feeling when a limb falls asleep, and can also be triggered by hitting your funny bone — what is it called?
Paresthesia: Dermal sensation with no physical cause.

Caused by a lack of intrinsic factor — often from an autoimmune attack on the stomach — this vitamin B12 deficiency disorder brings gradual fatigue, a smooth red tongue, and numbness in the hands and feet — which condition?
Pernicious anemia: Lack of red blood cells due to vitamin B12 deficiency.
Linked to prolonged sitting and excess hair, which skin condition causes a cyst to form between the cheeks of the buttocks and is treated with incision and drainage?
Pilonidal disease: Skin infection between the buttocks. Pilonidal disease is a type of skin infection that typically occurs as a cyst between the cheeks of the buttocks and often at the upper end.
Soft enough to slice with a knife, this silvery alkali metal carries the symbol K and takes its name from potash, the plant ashes it was first isolated from — what element is it?
Potassium: Chemical element with atomic number 19 (K)
Crossing the line between the natural and social sciences, this discipline scientifically studies the mind and behavior — both conscious and unconscious — in humans and other animals. What is it?
Psychology: Study of mental functions and behaviors.
Also marketed as canola once bred to lower its naturally high erucic acid content, this yellow-flowered Brassicaceae crop is the world's third-largest source of vegetable oil — which plant?
Rapeseed: Plant species grown for its oil-rich seed.
Usually caused by a vitamin-D deficiency, this childhood condition softens bones and can produce bowed legs and stunted growth — the adult analogue is osteomalacia; what is it?
Sold under the brand name Ventolin, this fast-acting inhaled medication opens the airways within about 15 minutes to treat asthma attacks and COPD — what is it?
Salbutamol: Short-acting bronchodilator used for acute asthma.
These marine algae include the kelps that shelter fisheries and are estimated to produce at least half of Earth's oxygen — what are they collectively called?
Seaweed: Macroscopic marine algae. Seaweed, or macroalgae, refers to thousands of species of macroscopic, multicellular, marine algae.

This Irish mathematician and physicist held Cambridge's Lucasian Professorship for an unmatched 54 years, leaving his name on equations of fluid mechanics and a theorem of vector calculus — who is it?
Sir George Stokes, 1st Baronet: British mathematician and physicist (1819–1903)
With eight legs, venom-injecting fangs, and silk-spinning spinnerets, this arthropod has spread to every continent but Antarctica — over 53,000 species and counting. What is it?
Signified by the minus sign, this arithmetic operation represents removing objects from a collection and is the inverse of addition — which operation is it?
Subtraction: One of the four basic arithmetic operations.
This daisy-family weed's yellow flowers give way to fluffy silver-tufted seed heads nicknamed 'clocks' or 'blowballs,' whose seeds scatter on the wind — which plant, better known by its common name?
Taraxacum officinale: Flowering plant species known as dandelion.
This French economist's best-selling 2013 book argued that capital returns persistently outpace economic growth, driving ever-rising wealth inequality — who is he?
Inside a ribosome, this cellular process reads messenger RNA three nucleotides at a time to build a chain of amino acids into protein — what is it called?
Translation (biology): Cellular process of protein synthesis. Translation is the process in biological cells in which proteins are produced using RNA molecules as templates.
RIKEN has been trying to synthesize this hypothetical element 119 since 2018 — the lightest element not yet made and the first of the eighth period. What is it?
Ununennium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 119 (Uue)

This Soviet cosmonaut commanded the first spaceflight to carry more than one crew member in 1964, then became the first human to die during a space mission when his parachute failed in 1967 — who was he?
Also called a slater or sow bug depending on region, this terrestrial crustacean is one of the few crustacean lineages to fully colonize dry land — what is it?
The symbol for chlorine is Cl. Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.
The symbol for zirconium is Zr. Zirconium is a chemical element; it has symbol Zr and atomic number 40.

Who among these is a comedian?
Arsenio Hall is a comedian. Arsenio Hall (born February 12, 1956) is an American comedian, actor and talk show host.
In what year was Truman Capote born?
Truman Capote: Capote had a troubled childhood caused by his parents' divorce, a long absence from his mother, and multiple moves.
In what year was Alec Baldwin born?
Alec Baldwin: Alexander Rae Baldwin III (born April 3, 1958) is an American actor and film producer.
In what year was Annette Bening born?
Annette Bening: Annette Carol Bening (born May 29, 1958) is an American actress.
In what year was Tom Selleck born?
Tom Selleck: Thomas William Selleck (born January 29, 1945) is an American actor.
In what year was Akshay Kumar born?
Akshay Kumar: Kumar is one of the most prolific actors in Indian cinema.
In what year was Judi Dench born?
Judi Dench: Dame Judith Olivia Dench (born 9 December 1934) is an English actress.
In what year was Jeffrey Dean Morgan born?
Jeffrey Dean Morgan (born April 22, 1966) is an American actor.
In what year was Josh Brolin born?
Josh Brolin: Josh James Brolin (born February 12, 1968) is an American actor and producer.
In what year was James Marsden born?
James Marsden: James Paul Marsden (born September 18, 1973) is an American actor.
In what year was Olivia Colman born?
Olivia Colman: A graduate of the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School, Colman's breakthrough came in the Channel 4 sitcom Peep Show (2003–2015).
